objective:
Create the machine-readable semantic regression corpus for this Android activity-logging app, and the Kotlin model + loader that reads it. This is test infrastructure: no production behaviour changes anywhere.

CONTEXT. The app turns a short sentence ("I cut the grass yesterday.") into a logged activity. The pipeline (all built and tested) is: `CandidateSelector` (core-domain, `select(catalog: List<CatalogActivity>, rawText): CandidateSelection`, bound `CandidateSelector.DEFAULT_BOUND` = 40) picks which existing activities to offer the on-device model; the model returns an `InterpretationCandidate` (core-domain `interpretation/InterpretationTypes.kt`: operation, activityResolution EXISTING_ACTIVITY/NEW_ACTIVITY/AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED, matchedActivityId, proposedCanonicalName, activityState COMPLETED/IN_PROGRESS or null, temporalExpression = the user's own time words, confidenceBand); `TemporalResolver` (core-domain `temporal/`) deterministically turns the time words into an Instant + `TimePrecision`; `InterpretationValidator` decides auto-accept vs review; `CaptureInterpretationOrchestrator` runs all of that and returns `AutoAccepted` / `NeedsReview(reasons)` / `Rejected(reasons)` / `InterpreterUnavailable`. `CatalogActivity(id, displayName, normalizedName, normalizedAliases, lastOccurredAt)` is in core-domain `repository/RepositoryTypes.kt`; `NameNormalizer` in core-domain `naming/` produces the normalized forms.

Later tasks (not this one) will (a) run every case through the real model on a phone and record its answers, (b) run it through a local stand-in model, and (c) replay recorded answers through the real orchestrator on the JVM and score them. So this corpus must be loadable from the CLASSPATH by: core-testing's own tests, an app-phone instrumented test (Android), and a core-ai host test. Put it at `core-testing/src/main/resources/semantic-corpus/corpus.json`.

BUILD:

1. **JSON library.** Add kotlinx.serialization (JSON) to `gradle/libs.versions.toml`: the runtime library, and the `org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization` Gradle plugin whose version is the existing `kotlin` version ref (2.3.21 -- Kotlin MUST NOT move off 2.3.x; see the catalog header). Verify the kotlinx-serialization-json version against Maven Central (e.g. fetch https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/jetbrains/kotlinx/kotlinx-serialization-json/maven-metadata.xml) and pick the newest release compatible with Kotlin 2.3.21 -- do not recall it from memory; state in your report what you checked. Declare the plugin `apply false` in the root `build.gradle.kts` next to the others, and apply it in `core-testing/build.gradle.kts` only. Expose the JSON library from core-testing as `api` only if a public signature needs it; otherwise `implementation`.

2. **Corpus model + loader** in `core-testing/src/main/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/`. `@Serializable` types for the corpus, a loader `SemanticCorpus.load(): SemanticCorpus` reading the classpath resource, a stable corpus hash (SHA-256 hex of the resource bytes) for later recordings to reference, and `catalogFor(case): List<CatalogActivity>` building the catalog with the fixture's FIXED ids (e.g. "act-mow-lawn"), normalized via `NameNormalizer`, `lastOccurredAt = null`. Keep the model plain and documented; later tasks build on it.

3. **Corpus shape.** Named catalog fixtures (reusable, fixed ids, display names, optional aliases) plus cases. Each case carries TEST_STRATEGY section 3 fields: `id` (stable, kebab-case), `category` (SYNONYM, NEAR_NEIGHBOUR, NEW_ACTIVITY, TEMPORAL, AMBIGUITY, STATE -- add others only if needed), `catalog` (fixture name), `rawText`, `capturedAt` (ISO offset datetime) and `zoneId`, and `expected`: `resolution`; `activityId` (catalog id) for EXISTING_ACTIVITY or `newActivityName` for NEW_ACTIVITY (plus `allowedNewNames` alternatives, compared after NameNormalizer); `state` with allowed alternatives (a sentence that does not say may legitimately yield null OR COMPLETED -- model that as a set); `temporalExpression` with `allowedTemporalExpressions` (null means the sentence gives no time); `resolvedLocalDate` + `precision` where a time is given; `mustNotMatch` (catalog ids); `outcome` = AUTO_ACCEPT or NEEDS_REVIEW. Optional `note` explaining why, for anything non-obvious.

   Expected values are the CORRECT PRODUCT BEHAVIOUR, not what any current model does. Principles (from the product spec): prefer an existing equivalent activity; never merge merely-related activities (a false merge corrupts history); new activity names are short, verb-first, one concept; copy the user's time words, never compute; when unclear, go to review rather than guess -- aggressive guessing is never rewarded.

4. **Cases (~40-50).** Use the fixed capture context 2026-09-15T20:00:00-04:00 / America/Detroit for all cases unless a case needs otherwise (2026-09-15 is a Tuesday). Must include, verbatim:
   - TEST_STRATEGY section 4 seed: Mow lawn equivalents "I mowed the lawn.", "I cut the grass.", "Finished mowing.", "Just mowed.", "I did the grass.", "The lawn is cut."; Edge lawn distinct "I edged the lawn.", "Finished edging.", "Did the lawn edges." (must not match Mow lawn); furnace filter "Changed the furnace filter.", "Replaced the HVAC filter.", "Put a new filter in the furnace.", "Swapped the air filter."; gutters "Cleaned the gutters.", "Cleared leaves out of the gutters.", "Did the gutters."; dryer vent "Cleaned the dryer vent.", "Cleared lint out of the dryer pipe."; plus generic dryer phrasing (e.g. "Cleaned the dryer.") that must NOT auto-accept Clean dryer vent.
   - TEST_STRATEGY section 5 temporal: "Mowed yesterday.", "Mowed this morning.", "Mowed Saturday.", "Mowed about an hour ago.", "Just finished mowing.", "Mowed on September 1st."
   - TEST_STRATEGY section 6 ambiguity: "Worked on the yard.", "Did the furnace thing.", "Handled the filter.", "Fixed that thing outside." -- all NEEDS_REVIEW, none may auto-accept anything.
   - AGENTS.md section 6: "cut the grass" matches Mow lawn (not a new activity); "edged the lawn" must not map to Mow lawn; "changed the furnace filter yesterday" resolves to yesterday, not today.
   - Near neighbours from the prompt's worked examples: raked leaves vs Blow leaves; washed the car vs Wax car -- with catalogs that make the point (neighbour present, equivalent absent => new activity, must not match the neighbour).
   - Edging against a catalog that has Mow lawn but NOT Edge lawn => NEW_ACTIVITY (name like "Edge lawn"), must not match Mow lawn. And edging against a catalog that has both => EXISTING Edge lawn.
   - New activity: e.g. "Flushed the water heater." against a catalog without it; and one case against an EMPTY catalog.
   - State: completed vs in progress ("I'm mowing now." => IN_PROGRESS).
   Design the catalog fixtures yourself (e.g. a standard household catalog of ~8-10 activities, a variant without Edge lawn, an empty one); keep each within the selector bound so every activity is offered.

5. **Corpus integrity tests** in `core-testing/src/test/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/`:
   a. Loads; case ids unique; every catalog reference exists; every activityId / mustNotMatch id exists in that case's catalog; each catalog within `CandidateSelector.DEFAULT_BOUND`; EXISTING_ACTIVITY cases have an activityId, NEW_ACTIVITY cases a newActivityName; AMBIGUITY cases expect NEEDS_REVIEW.
   b. Presence: every sentence listed in item 4's TEST_STRATEGY and AGENTS.md bullets appears (list them in the test; match case-insensitively on the sentence text; AGENTS.md phrases may be embedded in a longer sentence).
   c. Deterministic temporal check (hard): for every case with an expected temporalExpression, `TemporalResolver().resolve(expr, capturedAt, zone)` gives the expected local date (in the case's zone) and precision. Where the resolver's actual behaviour differs from the product-correct expectation, DO NOT change the resolver and DO NOT bend the expectation: mark the case with a `knownResolverGap` field describing the difference, and have the test assert that the set of gap cases is EXACTLY the marked set (so a later resolver fix, or a new regression, both fail the test loudly and visibly). Report each gap.
   d. `catalogFor` yields the fixed ids and NameNormalizer-normalized names.

STANDING RULES. Test infrastructure only. No change to core-domain, core-data, core-ai, app-phone, app-wear, or any production code; needing one is `scope_change_requested`. No logging/printing of corpus text from tests beyond assertion messages. Kotlin stays 2.3.21.
non_goals: No recording format, replay, scoring or report (SR1.2).
No device test, no stand-in model runner, no scripts (SR1.3, SR1.4).
No query corpus (TEST_STRATEGY section 7) -- needs the not-yet-built query interpreter.
Do not change TemporalResolver, CandidateSelector, the validator, the prompt or any production code, even to make a case pass.
Do not disable, @Ignore or weaken any existing test. Do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: kotlinx-serialization JSON library and the serialization plugin are in the version catalog; the plugin's version is the existing kotlin ref (2.3.21); the library version was verified against Maven Central (report says how); plugin declared apply-false in root build.gradle.kts and applied only in core-testing.

core-testing/src/main/resources/semantic-corpus/corpus.json exists and loads via a classpath loader in package com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.testing.corpus; a stable SHA-256 corpus hash is exposed.

Every case has id, category, catalog ref, rawText, capturedAt, zoneId and an expected block with resolution, activityId or newActivityName (+ allowed alternatives), allowed states, temporal expression + allowed alternatives + resolved local date + precision where a time is given, mustNotMatch, and outcome.

Corpus integrity test enforces: unique ids, valid catalog refs, every referenced activity id exists in its catalog, every catalog within CandidateSelector.DEFAULT_BOUND, resolution/field consistency, AMBIGUITY => NEEDS_REVIEW.

Presence test proves every TEST_STRATEGY section 4/5/6 sentence and the three AGENTS.md section 6 examples are in the corpus; near-neighbour, new-activity (incl. empty catalog), edging-without-Edge-lawn, generic dryer and in-progress cases exist.

Deterministic temporal test asserts TemporalResolver's local date and precision for every case with a time expression; any resolver gap is marked knownResolverGap on the case, the test asserts the gap set equals the marked set exactly, and the report lists each gap. TemporalResolver is unchanged.
catalogFor returns CatalogActivity entries with the fixture's fixed ids and NameNormalizer-normalized name/aliases.
No file outside write_paths changed (git status); no production module changed.
